x: It is hard to single out any one person, but special mention should be made of Len Marchant and Bill Bowers, both of whom have proved they are fast approaching the front rank of athletes by their fine performances.
Bill Bowers was another to show how much he is improving by winning the 220 yards. Fred White, who was making his last appearance for the Club owing to his being called for the R.A.F., finished 2nd.

There were no field events, it being a purely track meeting, and they had first and second string races with the 1 Mile and 3 Miles being run on the team principle. In the 100 Yards, Bill Bowers was third, with M.
Broadbent, the young Wallington schoolboy, in the sprints. In the 100 Yards, Bill Bowers ran extremely well, to be narrowly beaten by A.
Jones, and runners such as Bill Bowers, young Broadbent (who many of us would like to meet and wish well in his athletic career with the Club), Len Marchant, de Beau.

Tribute was paid to Percy by several members at the A.G.M., for his great work in keeping in touch with his fellow walkers through the " Belgrave News Letter." Bill Bowers, having passed his exams., is now a R.N. Signaller and posted to a ship in the Portsmouth area..
